review_method: Opus teacher-model review of a stratified 40-concept sample (largest 4 + random 4 per domain, seed=42), reading full representative prompt text -- not relying on the auto-generated name alone. See concept_review_sample.jsonl / concept_review_results.jsonl for the full per-concept record.

findings.finding: Two DNA Inheritance_Genomics concepts are genuinely too broad -- each merges distinct sub-topics (population genetics + transmission/linkage in one; meiosis + genome structure + sequencing in the other).
findings.recommendation: Candidates for a future finer re-split; not actioned in this pass -- see Definition of Done note on not optimizing for a particular concept count.

findings.finding: Two EMOTIONS concepts have auto-generated names drawn from shared instruction-template boilerplate ('answerable/prompt/provided/supplied'; 'stereotypes/relevant/state/internal') rather than the cluster's actual emotional content. The underlying cluster membership itself IS coherent -- only the TF-IDF naming heuristic was fooled by repeated scenario-template phrasing.
findings.recommendation: Treat provisional_name as unreliable for these two; rely on representative_prompt_texts directly.

findings.finding: A systemic naming weakness: many EMOTIONS/HINDI auto-names are polluted by residual function words (her, she, his; में, क्या, hai, mein, aur) that survived the stopword filter because the filter is English-only and does not cover Hindi function words or English pronouns comprehensively.
findings.recommendation: If concept names are consumed downstream, extend name_clusters.py's STOPWORDS list (English pronouns + a Hindi function-word list) before relying on provisional_name as a user-facing label.

findings.finding: HINDI domain clustering within several subdomains (Grammar, Vocabulary, Syntax) appears to split primarily by SCRIPT/language_form (romanized vs Devanagari rendering of similar content) rather than by distinct grammatical topic -- i.e. two 'concepts' in the same subdomain may be the same underlying topic expressed in two scripts, not two different topics.
findings.recommendation: Cross-reference with language_script_annotations.jsonl before treating HINDI concept boundaries as topic boundaries; this is a second, independent instance of the embedding space being more sensitive to surface form (script) than to content, consistent with Objective A's findings.

findings.finding: HINDI_Pragmatics_hdbscan_-1 is HDBSCAN's noise/outlier bin (label -1), not a genuine concept -- its content is topically coherent on inspection, but membership is a residual catch-all rather than evidence of a shared concept.
findings.recommendation: Flag any HDBSCAN label==-1 concept_id as review_status=uncertain in downstream consumption; not yet done automatically.

missing_coverage: Not assessed at full-corpus scale in this review pass (only the 40-concept sample was reviewed); domain_coverage.json's concepts_below_min_size and template_dominated_concepts lists are the automated proxy for coverage gaps.
ambiguous_assignments: Not separately tracked per-prompt in this pass; every prompt has exactly one concept assignment (confirmed by validate_taxonomy.py) and no multi-concept assignment mechanism was implemented, since the discovered clusters are a hard partition by construction (HDBSCAN noise aside, see above).
